messages.author: 3cfd637695216907
messages.subject: dplyr and dates
parts:
Hi all - 

I've been working with dates and have observed that dplyr is considerably slower when summarizing directly on a date column than when first converting to numeric. For example on my computer at work (late 2012 iMac, OS X Yosemite)

> df <- data.frame(group = sample.int(1e5, 1e6, replace=TRUE), date = as.Date("2014-01-01") + sample.int(10, 1e6, replace=TRUE))
> system.time({ df2 <- df %>% group_by(group) %>% summarise(min(date)) })
   user  system elapsed
  2.583   0.017   2.659
> system.time({ df2 <- df %>% mutate(date_num = as.numeric(date)) %>% group_by(group) %>% summarise(min(date_num)) })
   user  system elapsed
  0.862   0.007   0.889
> system.time({ df2 <- df %>% group_by(group) %>% mutate(date_num = as.numeric(date)) %>% summarise(min(date_num)) })
   user  system elapsed
  2.000   0.021   2.064

As per above if the numeric conversion is done after grouping instead of before, it's slower, I guess because as.numeric is invoked for every group and that's expensive. 
I've been converting to numeric each time for something like max/min, which is fine albeit a little clunky. Is there a better way, would writing my own hybrid handler help for things like this or other summary/mutate functions besides max/min? (I'm a total newbie to Rcpp.) 

Thanks! 

Andy
